units.passage: In such cases, instructors must directly explain to students why the process of achieving the specified learning outcomes for a class, without reliance on tools that create “shortcuts,” is integral to a student’s academic and personal growth. We recommend instructors consider three kinds of policies either for individual assignments or generally in their courses. To prohibit the use of GAI where it interferes with the student developing foundational understanding, skills, and knowledge needed for future courses and careers. To allow with attribution where GAI could be a useful resource, but the instructor needs to be aware of its use by the student and the student must learn to take responsibility for accuracy and correct attribution of GAI-generated content. To encourage and actively integrate GAI into the learning process where students can leverage GAI to focus on higher-level learning objectives, explore creative ideas, or otherwise enhance learning. Roadmap. We structure this report as follows.

Use of these tools will likely be very commonplace in X field and gaining experience in the ethical and efficient use of these tools will help you in your professional life once you have left the university. Required use This course will require the use of Generative AI tools for some (or all) assignments and assessments. Therefore, the use of these tools when instructed will not be considered a violation of academic standards. Students will be directed if and when citation or a statement-of-usage is needed. units.passage: Because AI tools often mimic human behavior, speech, and mannerisms, AI interacting directly with humans should disclose that its outputs or responses are machine-generated. In circumstances where AI is used such use shall be appropriately disclosed and transparent.
units.why: The Human-Informed principle says "such use shall be appropriately disclosed and transparent"; a binding disclosure duty for AI use, so P24, must, addressed to all.

units.passage: AI use in academic and professional work should be properly disclosed and cited.
units.why: 'AI use in academic and professional work should be properly disclosed and cited': general disclosure duty, P24.

units.passage: When AI is used in a substantive manner for analysis or decision-making (such as resume review, data analysis, grading, and other examples outlined in the AI Policy Supplement), faculty, staff, and students must follow the GSU Disclosure Standards detailed in the AI Policy Supplement.
units.policy: When AI is used in a substantive manner for analysis or decision-making, faculty, staff, and students must follow the GSU Disclosure Standards detailed in the AI Policy Supplement.
units.why: Substantive AI use "must follow the GSU Disclosure Standards" for faculty, staff and students; a mandatory disclosure rule, P24.

units.passage: Students should follow the disclosure instructions provided for each course and assignment.
units.why: "Students should follow the disclosure instructions provided for each course and assignment" is a disclosure rule, P24.

units.passage: How do you expect the GenAI applications to show up in citations (e.g. APA, Chicago, MLA, etc.)?
units.why: "How do you expect the GenAI applications to show up in citations (e.g. APA, Chicago, MLA, etc.)?" asks instructors to set how AI use is cited, matching P24 (disclose/cite AI use).

units.passage: As a baseline, always be honest and clear about how you’ve used AI in your work.
units.why: "always be honest and clear about how you’ve used AI in your work" is a baseline disclosure expectation, so P24, with should since it is phrased as a baseline.

units.passage: If you collaborate on any phase of an assignment, you must indicate what work is your own and what emerged from the collaboration
units.why: "If you collaborate on any phase of an assignment, you must indicate what work is your own and what emerged from the collaboration" requires attribution of assistance, which the policy later extends to AI. P24 (disclose with submission).

units.passage: Thus, to avoid plagiarizing, you must cite the source of any expressions, ideas, or observations not your own, whether they come from a primary source, a secondary source, an electronic source, a textbook, a class discussion, a lab manual, or any other source of information
units.why: "cite the source of any expressions, ideas, or observations not your own" is the general citation duty that, with the AI-specific clauses, applies to AI sources. P24.

units.passage: This includes assistance received from another person or from a Large Language Model or AI service.
units.policy: If there are no specific instructions, the ideas or work of others, including assistance received from a Large Language Model or AI service, must be clearly cited.
units.why: This passage says that where there are no specific instructions, assistance "from a Large Language Model or AI service" must be cited, and so extends the citation duty to LLM help. P24 because it is about acknowledging AI use; unit stance is permit because AI help is allowed once cited.

units.passage: It is good academic practice to acknowledge this assistance in a footnote or acknowledgments section offering thanks and describing the nature of the assistance.
units.why: The policy gives the method of acknowledgment, 'in a footnote or acknowledgments section' describing the nature of the assistance, framed as good practice. P24 (disclose with the submission), modality should; P25 asks for tool, prompt or output details, which are not required here.

units.passage: Quoting or paraphrasing language from a Large Language Model (LLM) or other AI service without citing this in the coursework you submit or present
units.why: The list of violations includes "Quoting or paraphrasing language from a Large Language Model (LLM) or other AI service without citing", making uncited AI text an academic honesty violation. P36 fits (classified as misconduct); P24 is about the duty to disclose, whereas this sentence classifies the failure as a violation.

units.passage: Transparent – use of AI is disclosed where appropriate
units.why: 'Transparent - use of AI is disclosed where appropriate' sits under 'All use must be:', so it requires disclosure of AI use where appropriate: P24, modality must, unit_stance require.
